audit.whatIsWrong: Every row of the chart disagrees with the already-audited mirror, and five of seven rows read 'Skill' as filler.
audit.why: The mirror (graves__urgot) set both layers to Skill / Graves / Graves / Urgot / Graves / Urgot / Urgot with ratings 5,6,6,4,6,4,3 on its side. Those tokens are champion names and read the same from either page, so this side takes the identical sides with inverted ratings (5,4,4,6,4,6,7). Every why that would have contradicted a flipped row is rewritten in the same proposal.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Graves / Graves / Urgot / Graves / Urgot / Urgot on both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is named on a dozen lines with no cooldown, and the page never says his ult exists as a spike.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s at 425 range and, critically, hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers that cooldown and refreshes its resistance boost — so it is not a fixed window. End of the Line is 13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s at 925, Smoke Screen 26/24/22/20/18s at 950, Collateral Damage 100/80/60s. Yours: Purge 12s down to no cooldown and no cost at rank 5 inside 490, Disdain 16s at rank 1, Fear Beyond Death 100/85/70s.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, the level whys and the content prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Buckshot' is used as an ability name in three places. It is not in Graves's kit. Also missing: Quickdraw grants armour and magic resist, and Smoke Screen reduces sight range rather than merely slowing.
audit.why: Graves's real abilities are New Destiny (P), End of the Line (Q), Smoke Screen (W), Quickdraw (E) and Collateral Damage (R). The dash doubling as a resistance buff is why trading into a fresh Quickdraw is bad, and the nearsight is why you must not throw Disdain blind — those are the two interactions that decide the fight.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name replaced with End of the Line and the shotgun's four-bullet spread; the resistance boost and the nearsight now stated in dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to engage 'on Quickdraw's cooldown' as though it were a fixed timer.
audit.why: Basic attacks lower Quickdraw's cooldown, so denying his autos is what actually keeps the window open.

edits.before: E or W second depending on kill pressure. A landed E-flip into W spray already wins most level-2 exchanges outright.
edits.after: E or W second by kill pressure, but a Quickdraw reset undoes a whiffed flip — Disdain is 16s and he only needs 425 to leave.

edits.before: Full legs rotation online — this is your lane now. Walk Graves down with W whenever Quickdraw is on cooldown.
edits.after: Full legs rotation online, but he pokes at 925 and Quickdraw steps out of your 490 — walk him down only once it is spent.

edits.before: Fear Beyond Death online — at 25% HP Graves is simply dead. Trade him to half, then the chain threat decides everything.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death needs him low first, while Collateral Damage is a 100s burst that lands on demand — his level 6 beats yours.

edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Quickdraw: 16s at rank 1, but every basic attack he lands shortens it — deny his autos and it stays down.

edits.before: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Quickdraw also grants armour and magic resist, so his dash doubles as defence — commit while it is down.

edits.before: Track Graves's Quickdraw: His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Flip + W shred.
edits.after: Smoke Screen nearsights you and is 26s at rank 1 — if you lose sight of him, hold Disdain rather than flipping blind.

edits.before: Level 2 favours you as you bait his shells and commit Q-W into his cooldowns.
edits.after: Level 2 favours him — Quickdraw resets let him burst and step out of Purge.

edits.before: Level 3-5 favours you since sustained trades beat his burst and your Q denies his kiting.
edits.after: Level 3 stays his — End of the Line pokes at 925 and Quickdraw leaves your range.

edits.before: Level 6 favours you because R flips and executes his Quickdraw all-in.
edits.after: Level 6 favours him — Collateral Damage is burst he can land on demand.

edits.before: First item favours Graves as an early lifesteal/lethality spike out-bursts you before you close.
edits.after: First item is yours: Black Cleaver and Sterak's out-grind his lethality burst in a long fight.

edits.before: Graves spikes hardest here — an early Eclipse or IE lifesteal item lets his Buckshot + smokescreen burst chunk you before you close, and his Quickdraw dash resets let him reposition out of your Q so his all-in briefly out-damages your sustain trade.
edits.after: Your first item is the swing: Black Cleaver stacks off every Purge tick and Sterak's covers his opening burst, so a Graves who has spent Quickdraw and End of the Line has to stand inside your 490 range and lose the long fight he did not want.

edits.before: Force extended trades after his Buckshot shells are on cooldown
edits.after: Force long trades once End of the Line (13s) is on cooldown

edits.before: Burst you with Buckshot + Smokescreen then Quickdraw out
edits.after: Burst with End of the Line + Smoke Screen, then dash out

edits.before: Level 1 is a skill lane — Graves' point-blank Buckshot hits hard but you have the frame to trade back with Echoing Flames autos, so respect the first shell and don't over-walk into a double-shot. From level 2-3 you tilt ahead: bait his Buckshot, then commit Q and W once his burst is down, because your sustained shred beats his cooldown-reliant damage.
edits.after: Level 1 is a skill lane — his shotgun hits hard point-blank but you have the frame to trade back with Echoing Flames autos, so respect the first burst and never over-walk into a full four-bullet spread. From level 2 he tilts ahead: End of the Line is 13s at rank 1 and pokes at 925, and Quickdraw steps straight back out of your 490 Purge range.

edits.before: Through levels 3-6 the lane is yours. Graves wants short, bursty trades and Quickdraw resets, but your Q slow-field cancels his kiting and your Purge grinds him down in any fight that lasts past his first rotation. At 6 your R is a clean punish — flip his aggressive Quickdraw entry and execute if he committed too low.
edits.after: Levels 3 to 6 seesaw. He owns 3 and 6 — End of the Line pokes at 925 and Collateral Damage lands burst on demand — while 4-5 are yours, because Purge grinds him down in any fight lasting past his first rotation. Land Corrosive Charge to pin him, then step into 490 range only once Quickdraw has been spent.

edits.before: First item is Graves' window: an early lifesteal/lethality spike lets his Buckshot and Smokescreen burst you before you engage, and his dash resets briefly let him out-trade and disengage. But with 2+ items you reclaim it — your bruiser HP pool and shred outlast his squishier profile, and R plus the leg execute punish a Graves forced to enter your range.
edits.after: First item is your window: Black Cleaver stacks off every Purge tick and Sterak's covers his opening burst, so once Quickdraw is spent he has to stand and lose the long fight. With 2+ items you stay ahead — your bruiser health pool and shred outlast his squishier profile, and R plus the leg execute punish a Graves forced to enter your range.
